sections.summary: The author explains his purpose and method: he has carefully investigated the events handed down by eyewitnesses and writes to give Theophilus certainty about what he has been taught.
The author introduces a righteous, Torah-observant priestly couple who are barren and advanced in years, setting up the pattern of divine intervention through humanly impossible circumstances.
While performing the incense offering in the temple, Zechariah encounters an angel of the Lord in the most liturgically authoritative setting possible for a divine communication.

Gabriel announces that Zechariah's son John will be a prophet in the spirit and power of Elijah, fulfilling Malachi's prophecy of a forerunner who will turn many of the sons of Israel back to the Lord and prepare a people ready for His coming.

Zechariah's disbelief in the face of Gabriel's announcement results in his being struck mute until the promise is fulfilled -- a disciplinary sign given as a consequence of unbelief in the most authoritative of settings.

sections.section_title: The People's Reaction and Elizabeth's Conception
sections.summary: The people realize Zechariah has seen a vision, Elizabeth conceives and interprets her conception as the Lord removing her disgrace, and the normal liturgical order of the temple is disrupted by a new act of God.
Gabriel announces to Mary that she will conceive a son who will be called the Son of the Most High, receive David's throne, reign over the house of Jacob forever, and have a kingdom without end.

sections.section_title: Mary's Question and the Angel's Answer
sections.summary: Gabriel explains the virginal conception through the Holy Spirit's overshadowing power, and Mary responds with complete availability to God's purpose, contrasting with Zechariah's earlier doubt.
Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, recognizes the unborn Jesus as 'my Lord' and pronounces Mary blessed for believing that what God promised would be fulfilled.

Mary's prophetic song declares God's characteristic pattern of reversing the fortunes of the proud and humble, the rich and hungry, grounding everything in God's faithfulness to the covenant promises made to Abraham and his descendants forever.

sections.section_title: The Birth and Naming of John
sections.summary: John is circumcised and named according to the angel's command, Zechariah's speech is restored at the moment of obedient compliance, and awe spreads through the hill country as people recognize the hand of the Lord on the child.

Zechariah, filled with the Holy Spirit, prophesies that God has visited and redeemed His people by raising up a Davidic deliverer, remembering the Abrahamic covenant oath, and sending John as the forerunner to give knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of sins.
John grows and becomes strong in spirit, living in the wilderness until the day of his public appearance to Israel.
